_comment: Ukkadam (Periyakulam) Lake water-quality benchmarks. Every numeric field carries its own provenance block. Values are PUBLISHED measurements, not modelled. The simulation does NOT consume these values: src/models/ecology.py integrates its own mass-conserving budget. This file exists for vetting, display and cross-checking only.

provenance.source: Gelera-Adefuin, M.J. (2019) IJITEE v8(6): Assessment of Water Quality and Parameters Leading to Eutrophication in an Urban Water Body (post-monsoon 2018-19, n=14)
provenance.note: Study area described as the Coimbatore Anicut channel system; model reference centre.

provenance.source: Gelera-Adefuin, M.J. (2019) IJITEE v8(6): Assessment of Water Quality and Parameters Leading to Eutrophication in an Urban Water Body (post-monsoon 2018-19, n=14)
provenance.quote: Ukkadam lake has a water spread area of 1.295 sq. km. and an average depth of 5.82m ... storage capacity of 70 mcft
provenance.note: Area x mean depth = 7.54 Mm3, inconsistent with 70 mcft (~1.98 Mm3) by ~3.8x. Both published figures retained; the model uses area and depth, and its oxygen budget is areal so it never consumes a volume.

sampling_design.method: boat-assisted surface sampling; Winkler titrimetry for DO; 5-day 20C incubation for BOD; potassium dichromate oxidation for COD

provenance.source: Gelera-Adefuin, M.J. (2019) IJITEE v8(6): Assessment of Water Quality and Parameters Leading to Eutrophication in an Urban Water Body (post-monsoon 2018-19, n=14)

provenance.note: CPCB Class C (freshwater fish culture) designates 4.0 mg/L as the minimum. Both studies agree the lake is normally ABOVE 4.0 mg/L in monsoon/post-monsoon; the lower bound is driven by temperature and organic load, not a chronic deficit.

floating_solar_ecological_constraints.rationale: Prevents photic-zone extinction, preserves light penetration for phytoplankton, and limits dissolved-oxygen deficits below the CPCB Class C minimum of 4.0 mg/L.

provenance.note: Policy cap adopted by this project; the 4.0 mg/L limit itself is the CPCB Class C standard recorded above.
